questions.enonce_markdown: the acceleration of the system and the tension in the string $PR$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** $P$ is on the table with $Q$ hanging over the pulley on the left and $R$ over the pulley on the right (Fig. 2). The strings are light and inextensible and the pulleys are smooth, so each string has a single tension throughout and all three blocks have the same acceleration $a$. Let $T_1 = 37.5\ \mathrm{N}$ be the tension in $PQ$ and $T_2$ the tension in $PR$; $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ (printed).

**Friction on $P$.** $P$ is in vertical equilibrium, so the normal reaction is $N = 2g = 20\ \mathrm{N}$. While $P$ is moving, friction is limiting:

$$F = \mu N = \tfrac12\times 20 = 10\ \mathrm{N}$$

**Direction of motion.** $P$ moves towards $R$. Suppose instead that it moved towards $Q$ with acceleration $a \ge 0$: then $R$ would rise, so $T_2 - 7g = 7a$, i.e. $T_2 \ge 70\ \mathrm{N}$, and for $P$, $T_1 - T_2 - 10 = 2a \ge 0$, i.e. $T_1 \ge 80\ \mathrm{N}$, which contradicts $T_1 = 37.5\ \mathrm{N}$. So the motion is towards $R$: $R$ descends, $Q$ ascends, and friction on $P$ acts towards $Q$.

**Equations of motion** (positive direction: $P$ towards $R$, $R$ downwards, $Q$ upwards):

- $R$: $\ 7g - T_2 = 7a \;\Rightarrow\; 70 - T_2 = 7a$
- $P$: $\ T_2 - T_1 - F = 2a \;\Rightarrow\; T_2 - 37.5 - 10 = 2a \;\Rightarrow\; T_2 = 47.5 + 2a$

Substituting the second into the first:

$$70 - 47.5 - 2a = 7a \;\Rightarrow\; 22.5 = 9a \;\Rightarrow\; a = 2.5$$

$$T_2 = 47.5 + 2(2.5) = 52.5$$

(Check with $R$: $70 - 52.5 = 17.5 = 7\times 2.5$.)

**The acceleration of the system is $2.5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ (with $R$ moving down) and the tension in the string $PR$ is $52.5\ \mathrm{N}$.**

For $Q$ (mass $m$, moving upwards with acceleration $a = 2.5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$), the tension $T_1 = 37.5\ \mathrm{N}$ acts upwards and the weight $mg$ downwards:

$$T_1 - mg = ma \;\Rightarrow\; 37.5 = m(g + a) = m(10 + 2.5) = 12.5\,m \;\Rightarrow\; m = 3$$

**The value of $m$ is $3\ \mathrm{kg}$.**

(Check: $R$ is heavier than $Q$, $7 > 3$, as the direction of motion requires; and the net driving force $7g - mg = 40\ \mathrm{N}$ exceeds the friction $10\ \mathrm{N}$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: $R$ strikes the horizontal ground $2$ seconds after release and does not rebound. Assuming that in their subsequent motion $P$ and $Q$ do not reach the pulleys, calculate the new acceleration of the system and the new tension in the string $PQ$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Speed when $R$ lands.** The system starts from rest, so after $2\ \mathrm{s}$: $\ v = u + at = 0 + 2.5\times 2 = 5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

**After $R$ lands.** $R$ stops and does not rebound, so the string $PR$ goes slack (no tension, because $P$ keeps moving towards the pulley of $R$). $P$ still moves towards $R$ at $5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $Q$ still moves upwards at $5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, so the string $PQ$ stays taut; let its tension be $T$ and the common acceleration $a'$ (positive in the direction of motion: $P$ towards $R$, $Q$ upwards). Friction on $P$ is still $10\ \mathrm{N}$, opposing the motion (towards $Q$), and $Q$ has mass $3\ \mathrm{kg}$.

- $Q$: $\ T - 3g = 3a' \;\Rightarrow\; T - 30 = 3a'$
- $P$: $\ -T - 10 = 2a'$ (tension and friction both oppose the motion)

Adding the two equations eliminates $T$:

$$-40 = 5a' \;\Rightarrow\; a' = -8$$

$$T = 30 + 3a' = 30 - 24 = 6$$

(Check with $P$: $-6 - 10 = -16 = 2\times(-8)$.) The tension is positive, so the string $PQ$ is indeed taut.

**The new acceleration is $-8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ (a retardation of $8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$) and the new tension in the string $PQ$ is $6\ \mathrm{N}$.** These values hold while $P$ moves towards $R$, i.e. for $\dfrac{5}{8}\ \mathrm{s}$, until the system is momentarily at rest.
